chunks: A number of our companions, from Saʿd ibn ʿAbdillāh, from Ayyūb ibn Nūḥ, who said:

I said to Abū al-Ḥasan al-Riḍā عليه السلام: “I hope that you are the Master of this affair, and that Allah will bring it to you without a sword, for allegiance has been pledged to you and the dirhams have been struck in your name.”

So he said: “There is none among us to whom letters are directed, who is pointed out with fingers, who is asked about the issues, and to whom wealth is carried, except that he is assassinated or dies upon his bed, until Allah sends for this affair a boy from among us, hidden in birth and upbringing, yet not hidden in his lineage.”

key_terms.الْأَمْوَالُ: funds or wealth carried to the Imam
key_terms.الْمَسَائِلِ: religious questions or issues brought for authoritative answer
key_terms.الْمَنْشَإِ: upbringing, development, or place/state of growing up
key_terms.صَاحِبَ هَذَا الْأَمْرِ: the divinely designated master of this matter, referring to the bearer of authority in this cause

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Riḍā عليه السلام say about the hidden birth of the Qaʾim from the Ahl al-Bayt?
ai.summary: This hadith records a statement of Imam al-Riḍā عليه السلام about the pattern of the Imams being recognized, sought out, and then removed, whether through assassination or death. It points forward to the one charged with this affair whose birth and upbringing would be concealed, while his noble lineage would remain known.
